newsitem.title: UK: Nat Grid welcomes court decision on pension.
newsitem.headline: Nat Grid welcomes court decision on pension.

text.p: British electricity transmission network National Grid Group Plc said on Tuesday it was pleased to note a court judgement in its favour over use of pension surpluses for redundancy payments.
In a statement, the company said it was "pleased to note the judgement...which allowed the appeals by (National Grid) against the final determinations of the pensions ombudsman".
It said the court statement said the effect of the decision was to "confirm the validity of the arrangements for dealing with surplus made by National Grid in 1993".
Mr Justice Robert Walker allowed an appeal by National Grid against a decision by Britain's pensions ombudsman that it should return 43 million stg.
The judge said the ombudsman's decision had been based on "a misunderstanding of the terms of the scheme and of the employers' duties in dealing with surplus."
He gave the two National Grid employees who had brought the case leave to appeal.
